Getting started: your first session

Everything you need for the first twenty minutes: starting a world, moving around, finding your pack and leaving without losing anything.

Voxelgame main dd29d91 · 7 min read · New players · feature ledger · all guides

Before you start

Voxelgame is played with a keyboard and mouse only. There is no gamepad support, and keys cannot be rebound. Keys are read by position, so on an AZERTY or other layout use the keys that sit where W A S D sit on a QWERTY keyboard. Keyboard, mouse and controller support

The window opens at 1280 × 720 and cannot be made smaller than 800 × 450. Press F11 or Alt + Enter to toggle borderless fullscreen; the game does not remember fullscreen between launches. Window, fullscreen and title

Good to know. Installing and updating the game is not covered by this guide yet; it is on the list of guides still to write. On Linux, an active Pinyin input method under X11 can swallow movement keys; that problem is unresolved in the game.

The start menu

Use Continue to enter the current world or Worlds to choose another. Settings, Credits, Study timer and Quit are also on the start menu. The current world name appears above the buttons. Start menu

Key or actionWhat it does
Up / Down arrowsMove the selection.
Enter or clickOpen the selected entry.
EscGo back from any sub-page to the first page.
POpen the Study Grove focus timer (not while typing on the Worlds page).
  • Continue enters the current world.
  • Worlds lists your saved worlds and creates new ones (next section).
  • Settings opens the same settings panel you get in a world by pressing Esc.
  • Credits shows seven title cards on a black stage: the maker, thanks and a dedication. Each card stays for 12 seconds and the set loops. Press Esc, Enter or Space, or choose Skip credits, to go back. There are no Previous or Next buttons yet. The normal music playlist keeps playing.
Tip. The first launch shows a tumbling wireframe cube while the world loads. Later loads show only a stage text and an activity bar.

Create your first world

  1. Choose Worlds on the start menu.
  2. Type a name. Typing both filters the list of saved worlds and names the world you are about to create.
  3. Choose Create world, or press Enter while that row is selected.
  4. Wait for the world to load; you arrive standing on the starting island.

New worlds always open in creative mode: there is no seed, mode or difficulty picker. Every new world's pack already holds 12 Berries, 2 Water flasks, 1 Empty flask and 4 Alder board pieces. New worlds: creative by default, survival starter supplies

Good to know. The Worlds page shows only four rows at a time and the mouse wheel does not scroll it. Use the Up and Down arrows or type to filter. Each row shows the picture of that world's last visit. Rename and backups are not in the game yet. Worlds: create, load, search and delete
Tip. To keep a world near the top, click the star at the left of its row, or press Tab with the row selected. Starred worlds are listed right after the current world. Choose Starred (or press Shift+Tab) to show only starred worlds. Stars are saved in the worlds folder, not in the world.
Careful. To delete a world, hold its DELETE badge, or hold the Delete key with the row selected, for 3 seconds. The world you are currently in cannot be deleted.

Look and move

Click the world once to capture the mouse. That first click never mines or places a block. While the mouse is released (after opening a panel, pressing Esc, or switching away from the window) you cannot move or look. Closing a panel captures the mouse again on its own. Mouse capture and release

Key or actionWhat it does
W / A / S / DWalk forward, left, back, right (about 4.3 m/s). You step up half-metre blocks without jumping.
MouseLook around.
SpaceJump about 1.25 m; hold it to jump again on every landing. A full one-metre block needs a jump.
Shift (hold)Sneak at about 1.3 m/s; you cannot walk off an edge while sneaking.
Ctrl + W (hold)Sprint at about 5.6 m/s.
CCrawl through gaps 0.6 m tall; press C or Space again to stand.
F or double-tap SpaceStart or stop flying (creative only). Space rises, Shift descends, Ctrl boosts.

Walking speeds do not depend on frame rate, because movement runs on a fixed 60 Hz step. Walking and looking around

Tip. Print Screen releases the mouse so that you can use a system screenshot tool. The game itself has no screenshot key.

Read the screen

  • Top left: the status line. Actions report here, for example 'Collected … ×3' or 'Capacity full; block left behind'.
  • Top right, left of the map: the looking-at card, shown when you aim at a block within 6 m. F2 hides or shows it, the same as Settings > General > Target info.
  • Top right: the compact map, with the FPS and coordinates box beneath it. The box is on by default; turn it off in Settings > Debug.
  • Lower right: the collection feed. It shows what you gained, for example '+3 Oak wood', for a few seconds. Crafting, creative mining and home storage do not show there.
  • Middle: the crosshair, and a small action hint under it.
  • Lower left (survival only): the four bars for health, hunger, thirst and stamina.
  • Bottom: the ten-slot hotbar and the label of the selected item.

Press F1 to hide the whole HUD, the crosshair and your hands, for example before a screenshot; press it again to bring everything back. HUD overview Clean view (F1)

Open your pack and the hotbar

Press E to open the inventory and press it again to close it. The tabs are Pack, Craft, Home and Journal in survival, plus Build in creative; switch with the mouse, Tab or Shift + Tab. The header always shows how much you carry out of 1000 capacity. The Pack tab lists carried items as icons with quantity numbers; hover an icon to see its name. Inventory screen and its tabs

The hotbar

The hotbar has ten slots that start empty. A slot is a shortcut to an item kind, not a container, so its number is everything of that kind in your pack.

Key or actionWhat it does
1 – 9, 0Select slot 1 to 10.
Mouse wheel, [ and ]Cycle through the slots.
Hover an item + 1 – 9 or 0Bind that item to the slot (inventory open).
Drag an item onto a slotBind it. Dragging a slot onto another swaps them; dragging a slot off the bar clears it.

With the inventory closed, Tab cycles through the tools and weapons you carry and back to empty hands. Bindings are saved with the world. Ten-slot hotbar

Creative and survival

There are exactly two modes. Press F4 to switch, except on the start menu, in Study Grove or while connected to a server; your pack, hotbar and position stay as they are, and each world remembers the mode you left it in. Creative and survival modes (F4)

Creative

  • Blocks break instantly and placing is free; crafting is free.
  • The Build tab and catalog, middle-click block picking, building brushes and undo.
  • Flight, map travel and teleport.
  • Editable time, weather and season.

Survival

  • Blocks take time to mine and your pack is limited to 1000 capacity.
  • Four bars for health, hunger, thirst and stamina, shown lower left.
  • Falls hurt, and you eat with R, drink with T and quick-craft with X.
  • Dying returns you to your rest point and loses nothing.

Items you took from the creative catalog stay in your pack after you switch to survival. Continue with Your first survival day.

Pause, save and quit

Press Esc in the world to open Settings. The game pauses and the panel is titled 'Paused'. Esc first closes anything that is open (the pack, the large map, Study Grove), and only opens Settings when nothing is. The General tab also has Speed FOV (widens the view at high speed), Damage bob (Off, Reduced or Full camera dip when hurt) and Target info. Settings menu basics Esc key and what pauses the game

Key or actionWhat it does
EscOpen Settings and release the mouse; press it again to close.
F6Save the world right now ('World saved safely').
Settings > Main menuSave and return to the start menu.
Ctrl + Q, Save & quit or the window's close buttonSave, then quit. If saving fails, the game stays open.

The world also autosaves about every 30 seconds whenever it has unsaved changes. Settings are stored inside each world's save, so loading another world brings back that world's settings. Saving, Main menu and quitting

How this guide was checked

Every key, number and message below was read from the game source at the audited commit and traced to a ledger entry. The four screenshots come from the same commit's release build, run headless against a throwaway world. The Target info, Speed FOV and Damage bob settings were checked against game commit 6acf338 (main 4bd6541), which came after the audited commit.
